text.p: The unlisted investeerimispank is looking for a foreign buyer and is interested in selling up to 100 percent of its shares, Aripaev newspaper said on Wednesday.

Maria-Luisa Cicognani, who represents the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on the board of Investeerimispank, was quoted as saying that the board is looking for a strategic foreign investor to buy 100 percent of its shares.

The bank's stock is currenly held by the Bank of Estonia with 33 percent, EBRD with 33 percent, Swedfund with 11 percent, Finnfund with 11 percent, and Deutsche Investitions- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft with 11 percent.
The small bank's 1996 profit was 10 million kroons, Aripaev said.
